paragraphs: R’ Yochanan ben Torta. (A Tanna, a colleague of R’ Akiva.)

Hyman cites [Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.4.5.13) (folio 21a): when R’ Akiva called Ben Koziva the King Messiah, R’ Yochanan ben Torta told him, “Akiva, grass will grow on your cheeks, and the son of David will still not have come.” Hyman also cites ש״ר at the beginning of chapter 1 for the episode found in [Shemot Rabbah 40:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Shemot_Rabbah.40.1). Yochanan comes before R’ Akiva, who tells him, “Stand and read the Torah.” He replies, “I have not reviewed the portion,” and the Sages praise him. [Yoma 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.9a.6) preserves his explanation that Shiloh was destroyed because of contempt for sacred things and forbidden sexual relations. Hyman cites Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:10 for the saying found at [7:10 in the consulted text](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.7.10.1): even after a person dies, his lips move in the grave.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The “21a” following Taanit 4:5 is a folio number. Hyman’s printed abbreviation for the Torah-reading story is ש״ר רפ״א.

The linked Taanit puts the negation in brackets. The linked Torah-reading exchange is in Shemot Rabbah 40:1, where Akiva addresses Yochanan and Yochanan answers those present. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1857&lang=en) also places the story at the beginning of chapter 40.

The [continuation in Yoma 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.9b.1-2) explains the two reasons given for Shiloh’s destruction. The linked Shir HaShirim Rabbah has the saying about lips moving in the grave under Yochanan ben Tortah (תורתה), at 7:10 rather than Hyman’s 4:10.
